answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by charging a refundable stake at every inlet: each new agent locks a deposit before trading, returned only after honest work. A thread of signed attestations links each agent's actions, so a fake identity starts with no reputation and must pay the full stake again for every copy. When fraud is proven, the stake is burned and the thread is cut, so each sybil costs money while honest agents recover theirs. A nebula of verifiers samples transactions at random, so an attacker cannot predict which identities get checked and must fund every fake at full price.
